recent.title: Under the Iron Sky
recent.author: A.T. Emerald
recent.review: there's something deeply concerning about how i always get attached to worlds where survival apparently requires doing the most HORRIFIC things. yet here i am , having the time of my life while practically everyone in under the iron sky is fighting for theirs. i swear there's just something about a dark , dystopian world that scratches a very specific itch in my brain and this one absolutely delivereddd. soraya and ikarus are exactly the kind of morally grey characters i love. neither of them are innocent and they've both done some pretty terrible things , but in their minds , everything's justified if it means protecting the people they care about. what i found especially interesting was watching their entire understanding of each other's worlds slowly fall apart. they'd both been fed so many lies about the other side that seeing them gradually question everything they thought they knew was SO satisfying. especially soraya , as she started seeing how differently things actually worked outside of everything she'd been taught to believe. ughh i put this review off for so long bc its... complicated. this book is around 540 pages and i genuinely don't think the pacing was bad at all. i wasn't bored , i never felt the urge to skim through chapters and i was invested. BUTTT when i actually sat down and thought about everything that happened after finishing , uhh like not that much happened ?? like yes , soraya gets captured , we learn about the world and slowly uncover all these secrets , but that's essentially where a HUGE portion of the book goes. i get it. this is the first book in a trilogy and there's only so much you can reveal. but i would've loved to spend more time exploring the other characters and their perspectives instead of being so heavily focused on soraya's captivity. especially knowing what we know after what happened towards the end. there's so much more i wish we'd gotten to see and i can only hope book two gives us some of that. THE GOOD : THAT ENDING. oh i fearrr we're in for something absolutely insane with the sequel. there's so much that could happen now that everything is finally out in the open and considering who they're going up against... yeah , i'm a little worried for everyone involved. but i have faith in them. whether that faith is going to get me anywhere is an entirely different question. i keep thinking about how i went from giving half city 3.5 stars to absolutely LOSING it over cursed city. idk , i'm getting a similar feeling here. we've spent so much time getting to know this world and its characters that i feel like we've barely scratched the surface of what this story could become. and with everything that's happened towards the end , i genuinely think book two has the potential to take everything i already loved about this one and make it SO much better. at least that's what i'm hoping for because i am NOT ready to let go of these characters just yet. now excuse meee while i wait for december so i can fight for the fairyloot edition. the math is mathing on this one unfortunately.

recent.title: Victorious
recent.author: V.E. Schwab
recent.review: how exactly am i supposed to say goodbye to an entire cast of characters that i've grown THIS attached to ?? because i'm still sitting here trying to process the fact that it's actually over. like that's it ?? we're DONE ?! excuse mee while i go through the five stages of grief. i've known about this series like forever but only managed to bully myself into picking up vicious a couple of months ago. anddd of course , it was an immediate five stars. i fell in love with these characters SO insanely quickly and somehow became even more attached as the series went on. vengeful gave me so much more insight into eli's past , his childhood and everything that shaped him into the person we know , which was honestly one of my FAVORITE parts of that book. i absolutely adore getting inside a character's head like that , especially someone as morally complicated as eli. which is also why i was a little disappointed with how his storyline was handled towards the end. after spending so much time exploring his past and understanding him on a much deeper level , i really wanted a little more time with his character before everything came together. it was one of the only things that kept vengeful at a 4.5 star for me. then there's victorious. OH MY GOD. i absolutely DEVOURED this book. despite being ridiculously busy with family and friends , i managed to fly through it in just a couple of days and honestly never even felt its length. i was so invested in everything happening that putting it down felt like an actual inconvenience. i literally spent so much time imagining all the different ways schwab could possibly wrap up this trilogy before even picking it up , and somehow she managed to take it in a direction that NEVER once crossed my mind. like out of every possible scenario i'd come up with , THIS was not one of them. and honestly , i was so pleasantly surprised by how everything unfolded. but that ending... yeah. i have a LOT of feelings about that ending. the thing is , i understand it. i understand why things had to happen the way they did and why certain characters made the decisions they made. it makes sense for the story and i can appreciate that. but there's also this incredibly selfish part of me that wanted something more for them. i think i'd gotten so attached to this little family that i had already started imagining victor , mitch , sydney and of course , dol getting to live some version of a normal life together. after everything they'd been through , i just wanted them to have that. and i KNOW that's probably asking for a little too much from a trilogy like this , especially knowing the kind of people we're dealing with here , but damn. i wanted that for them so badly. and even though i can understand and appreciate the way schwab chose to end their stories , it doesn't make saying goodbye even a tiny bit easier. i think that's why i'm keeping this at 4.75 rather than giving it the full five stars. not because the ending was badly written or because i didn't appreciate it , but because some part of me is still desperately holding onto the ending i wanted for these characters. i'm just not ready to let them go yet. this trilogy has genuinely become one of my favorites and i would HAPPILY read another thousand books about victor , sydney , mitch and this entire morally questionable family. i'm so glad i finally gave vicious a chance because i really had no idea just how much these characters would come to mean to me. and as excited as i am to explore more of schwab's work , i already know i'm going to miss this world terribly. this book gave me so much and somehow still left me wanting more. maybe that's what makes saying goodbye so difficult.

recent.title: Kiss Slay Replay
recent.author: Rachel   Harrison
recent.review: tell me why reading this felt like playing until dawn except every time i thought i'd figured out what was coming , rachel harrison decided to throw an ENTIRELY different nightmare at me. like seriously , zombies , phantoms , cryptids... at this point i'm convinced there's NOTHING that isn't trying to kill these people. that's exactly why i think she deserves some credit here. there's a reason why we don't see many time loop novels and it's plainly because , they are notoriously difficult to pull off. there's only so many times you can make someone relive the same day before it starts getting repetitive and very boring. but somehow , that never really happened here. every loop had something new going on and i was always curious to see what fresh hell we'd be dealing with next. there's just SO much happening in this book and i love that she managed to keep things entertaining without making the whole time loop concept feel like a chore to get through. what i didn't expect was how much i'd appreciate willa's character development. and i'm NOT about to sit here giving a whole lecture about life lessons because who am i kidding , i came here for the horror. but i really did love seeing how much she'd changed from the beginning to the end , especially when it came to finally confronting the things she'd been running away from. it was such a satisfying part of the story and honestly , i didn't expect to care about that nearly as much as i did. NOW... can we PLEASE talk about that ending because after everything this book put us through , THAT'S how we're wrapping things up ?! i'm sorry but i was expecting something a little more unhinged after spending an entire book getting terrorized by practically every supernatural creature known to mankind. instead , everything felt a little too easy and honestly quite anticlimactic. like i get what the ending was trying to do , but WHERE was the final round of absolute insanity ?? i was fully prepared for things to get so much worse. ANYWAYSS , i promise i actually liked this book LMAOO. the way i've been going on about that ending you'd think i hated the entire thing when i genuinely had so much fun reading it. i just wish the finale had matched the insanity of everything that came before it because i was SO ready for things to go completely off the rails. regardless , i'll definitely be reading more from rachel harrison.

recent.title: The Poet Empress
recent.author: Shen Tao
recent.review: i finished this a few days ago and i STILL don't think i've fully recovered. this was an immediate five star read , possibly even six , because apparently i've developed a habit of falling in love with books that leave me completely hollow. and this one... yeah. this book sank its blades into me and absolutely REFUSED to let go. the funniest part is that i was actually TERRIFIED to pick this up. after dnfing the unicorn hunters , seeing "political fantasy" in the tags was enough to make me question whether i'd even enjoy this. my illumicrate copy had been sitting on my shelf for MONTHS until i randomly came across a few tiktoks calling it one of the best books of the year and decided to give it a chance. ON HALLOWEEKEND OF ALL TIMES. i genuinely thought there was no way i'd be finishing this anytime soon because i had SO much going on , between going out with friends , celebrating halloween and everything else i had planned. reading was probably the last thing i expected to have time for. WELL... none of that mattered because i was hooked from the very first chapter and somehow managed to read almost 300 pages on friday alone before finishing the rest on halloween. TWO DAYS. during one of the busiest weekends i've had in a while. i genuinely could NOT put this thing down. the court politics ended up being one of my FAVORITE parts of this entire book which is actually hilarious considering how much i was dreading them. the tension , the calculated power plays , the constant feeling that one wrong move could completely ruin someone. I LOVED IT ALL. everyone wants a piece of power and absolutely nobody is above doing whatever it takes to get it. every conversation felt like someone was inches away from walking into a trap and i was eating up every second of it. and TERREN... oh my god. here's someone who appears so cold , cruel and almost irredeemable on the outside , but the more you learn about him , the more you realize just how badly the very system he was born into failed him. he's such a morally gray character and i LOVE that about him. it doesn't excuse everything he's done , but damn does it make his character so much more heartbreaking. he was exploited by the very people that were supposed to protect him , right until the very end. how am i NOT supposed to sympathize with him after everything he's been through ?? genuinely one of the best MMCs i've read about in a LONG time. WEI THOUGH. i absolutely ADORE her. it's been so long since i've read a book where i can confidently say that i loved BOTH of the main characters this much. like genuinely , i don't think there's a single thing i'd change about either of them. their complexity , their development , the decisions they make and everything they have to endure... i just wanted to reach into the pages and give them both a hug. and the two of them together ?? perfect for each other in another life , FOR REAL. i'm actually going to cry again if i think about this for too long. i read and watch a LOT of horror , and i think i've become pretty desensitized to disturbing things at this point. especially with everything happening in the world right now , where we're constantly exposed to increasingly horrific things that people are capable of doing to each other. sometimes even the most disturbing things in fiction barely faze me anymore , which is why i've always said that if a book manages to make me emotional or even tear up , it's immediately entering my six star territory. AND THIS BOOK DID SO MUCH WORSE. i was literally sitting there begging for things to turn out okay because i could NOT handle watching these characters suffer anymore. and of course , every time i thought things couldn't possibly get more devastating , something else would happen and i'd be right back to questioning why i willingly put myself through this. that ending !! i don't even know whether to call it happy or sad. bittersweet is probably the closest i'll ever get because it somehow managed to leave me feeling relieved and absolutely HEARTBROKEN at the same time. i could literally write an entire essay about how much i love this book and STILL not have enough words to explain it. the characters , the writing , the storytelling... it all came together so beautifully and i honestly don't think i could've asked for more. and the fact that this is a DEBUT is actually INSANE to me. shen tao , you've absolutely outdone yourself because WHAT A BOOK. i'm so glad i finally picked this up after putting it off for so long because this was easily one of the best reading decisions i've made all year. (six stars in my heart because five is simply NOT enough)
